 Judgment

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 25.09.2018 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal ( 'MACT' for short), Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru, in MVC No.4580/2017.
2.
This appeal is premised on the ground of inadequacy of compensation.

3. The brief facts of the case are as under:
On 23.02.2017, the claimant-Smt, Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi was traveling in APSRTC Bus bearing No.AP.04.Y.6715 on NH-42 as an inmate passenger.

While the said bus was being driven at about 01.15 p.m., near Kalupalli Village, Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, Andhra Pradesh, the driver of the said bus drove the bus with high speed and in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety and dashed against the on-coming lorry bearing Registration No.
TN.28.AR.4129, as a result of which, claimant sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately thereafter, claimant was shifted to Palamner Government Hospital,
where she was treated as an inpatient and thereafter she was shifted to CMC Hospital at Vellur, where she obtained treatment as an inpatient.
Thereafter, she was discharged with an advise to take regular follow-up treatment.

It is the case of the Smt. Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi vs The National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98931947/
2 claimant that, while being inpatient, she spent lot of money for her treatment and due to the accident, she has suffered permanent disability affecting her future earning capacity and her day-to- day functional capacity.

sentences.text:
She further states that, due to the injuries suffered in the said accident, she is unable to do her regular work, as she was able to do prior to occurrence of accident and in view of the injuries suffered by her in the accident in question, she filed a claim petition seeking compensation,
against the respondents.
4. On service of notice, the respondents appeared and filed their detailed statement of objections.
However, Respondent No.2 did not represent despite service of notice and was placed ex-parte.
Respondent No.1 took-up a plea inter alia denying issuance of Insurance Policy and further contended that, the liability if any, would be in terms of the conditions of the policy.

It was further pleaded that, the accident in question has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of APSRTC Bus and that a false case is filed against driver of the bus by colluding with the jurisdictional police.

It is also pleaded that the driver of offending vehicle was not having a valid and effective Driving Licence as on the date of occurrence of accident in question and that the driver of the offending vehicle has violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Whereas, Respondent No.3 in the statement of objections has denied occurrence of accident due to the rash and negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

However, he admitted that he had hired the offending vehicle viz., the APSRTC Bus, belonging to Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the vehicle and the same was insured with the 1st respondent and the Insurance Policy was valid as on the date of occurrence of accident in question.

It is further pleaded that, if at all any liability would be fastened,
it has to be on Respondent No.1-Insurance Company, with which the insurance policy was in force.
It is also contended by Respondent No.3 that the claim petition is liable to be dismissed for mis-joinder and non-joinder of necessary and proper parties.
5. On the basis of the said pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal has framed the relevant issues for consideration.
6. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimant examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Eleven documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

The claimant also examined the Doctor by name Dr. Shivaprakash as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P11 to P14.
7.
On the other hand, the respondent examined one M.Dasharatha as RW.1, who is the driver of APSRTC Bus.
But, however he did not produce any documents on their behalf.

8. Having heard the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and on perusing the material documents placed before the Court both oral and documentary, the Tribunal passed an award granting compensation of Rs.2,99,200/- with interest at the rate of 8% per annum and held Respondents No.1 to 3 to be liable jointly and severally to pay compensation.

However, in view of the Insurance Policy being in force, Respondent No.1, who is the insurer of offending vehicle, was directed to deposit the compensation amount Smt. Saraswathi @ K. sentences.text:
Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellant/claimant and the learned counsel for the respondent/Insurer and the Respondent-APSRTC Corporation, the point that would arise before this Court is, -
"Whether the judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is meager and calling for interference by this Court,, and whether enhancement is warranted in the present facts and circumstances of this case."

10. It is not in dispute that the accident in question has occurred on 23.02.2017 while the claimant was traveling in APSRTC Bus, which met with an accident by colliding with a lorry which came from opposite direction, due to which the claimant sustained serious injuries and though she having undergone treatment, has suffered certain disabilities as per the opinion of the Doctor (PW.2) and also having produced necessary documents to that effect with regard to Exs.P11 to P15, the liability,
rashness and negligent driving has been attributed to the driver of the APSRTC Bus, which is evidenced by production of Exs.P1 to P6, which are the police records, the same is not disputed or challenged.

In view of the liability not being seriously challenged and there being no cross-appeal or cross-objection preferred either by insurer or APSRTC Corporation, this Court does not want to delve into the correctness of accident and the liability fastened, and so also some of the injuries sustained by the claimant due to the accident.

However, the learned counsel for the Insurer-Respondent No.1 has seriously disputed the disability to an extent of 28% opined by the Doctor, it affirms the judgment and award made by the Tribunal with regard to calculation of disability at 8%.

11. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation and income, it is also not seriously disputed with regard to the age of the injured being 55 years and the appropriate multiplier having been taken by the Tribunal being '11' is also not in serious dispute.

Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with the judgment and award of the Tribunal with regard to assessment of age of '55' years and the multiplier of '11' being applied.
12.

Learned counsel for the appellant/claimant has vehemently contended that the Tribunal has grossly erred in assessing meager income of Rs.8,000/- per month without appreciating the material evidence placed on record.
Admittedly, in the case on hand, no material in proof of income has been placed by the claimant.
In the absence of the same, the Tribunal has assessed the income to be at Rs.8,000/- per month.

13. I am in agreement with the learned counsel for the appellant/claimant that the assessment of income made by the Tribunal is on the lower side and the same calls for interference by this Court for the reason that, in the absence of proof of income, the Tribunal and this Court are left with no other alternative, but to do standard guess work.
The Karnataka Legal Services Authority has formulated Notional Income Chart prescribing income for relevant year of accident.
Admittedly, in the case on hand, the accident having occurred in the year 2017, the Notional Income Chart prescribes Rs.11,000/- to be taken as an income for the said year.
Accordingly, I deem it appropriate to take the income of the claimant in the present case at Rs.11,000/- per month, as against Rs.8,000/- per month adopted by the Tribunal.

sentences.text: The claimant has also got examined the Doctor as PW.2, who has deposed before the Court by stating that, the claimant has suffered disability to an extent of 28% to the whole body.

He has opined that, on clinical examination he found that the claimant has suffered a blunt trauma injury to neck and maxillary region and amputation of middle pharynx of left middle finger, and she is having difficulty in opening the mouth, hoarseness of voice and difficulty in speaking and in deglutition.
Calculating all these injuries, the Doctor-PW.2 has assessed the disability to the whole body at 28%.

However, it is brought to the notice of this Court that, in the wound certificate produced at Ex.P3,
there is no mention with regard to injury of fracture as canvassed by the learned counsels appearing for the APSRTC and Insurance Company.
However, the wound certificate at Ex.P3 shows that there is a head injury and multiple fractures.
On a careful assessment of the injuries suffered by the claimant, the Tribunal has assessed the disability to an extent of 8% by deducting 1/3rd towards the whole body disability.

Even if 28% disability is taken on the basis of clinical assessment made by the Doctor- PW.2, after taking 1/3rd of total disability, each portion of it would be at 9.3%, which is to be considered as whole body disability.
Whereas the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 8%.
Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that, the whole body disability assessed by the Tribunal at 8% is on the lower side.

15. Considering the fact that the claimant has lost her middle finger and she is unable to do her work as she was doing prior to the accident, I deem it appropriate to take the disability at 10% to the whole body.

Therefore, the loss of future earning capacity on the basis of the disability at 10% to whole body, the income to be assessed by this Court would be Rs.1,45,200/-
[Rs.11,000x12x11x10/100], as against Rs.84,480/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. Under the head of 'Pain and Suffering', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.
It is not in dispute that the claimant was inpatient for a period of 11 days.
Having suffered injuries to her head and other parts of the body, it is not possible for this Court to assess the mental trauma and agony undergone by the claimant.
However, some reasonable amount will have to be awarded as a solace to the pain and suffering undergone by the claimant.
Therefore, I deem it proper to enhance the amount under this head, to Rs.50,000/- as against Rs.30,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

17. Towards 'Medical Expenses' the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,28,716/-, which is on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant at Ex.P7 and the same does not call for interference by this Court.
Hence, the same is retained.
18. Towards 'Loss of income during laid-up period', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.16,000/-.

In view of this Court having enhanced the monthly income of the claimant from Rs.8,000/- to Rs.11,000/-
and three months time would be required for the claimant to recuperate and get back to her normal day-to-day activities, Rs.33,000/- is awarded under this head, as against Rs.16,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
19. Towards 'Future Amenities and Happiness', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- and in my opinion, it is on the lower Side.
Hence, I deem it proper to enhance the compensation under this head by another sum of Rs.20,000/-, by making it Rs.40,000/-

Smt . Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi vs The National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98931947/
5 20.

sentences.text: Towards 'Attendant Charges, Conveyance, Food and Nourishment charges, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.
I do not find any legal infirmity in the said compensation awarded.

Hence,
the same is retained and not interfered with.
21. Towards 'Future Medical Expenses' the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.
The claimant has not placed any material before this Court to show that she would require treatment in future either by herself or through the evidence of the Doctor-PW.2.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Hence, the compensation amount awarded under this head is not disturbed.
22. In view of the discussions made herein above, the claimant is entitled for revised compensation as mentioned in the table below:

3 Loss of income during laid-up 33,000-00  period
4 Loss of future income 1,45,200-00  5 Loss of future amenities and  happiness 40,000-00  6
Attendant, conveyance, food  and nourishment charges 20,000-00  7 Future Medical Expenses 20,000-00
Total 4,36,916-00  (-)Minus the amount 2,99,196-00  awarded by the Tribunal  Enhanced Compensation 1,37,720-00  amount 23. Accordingly, I pass the following order:
ORDER i) The appeal preferred by the appellant/claimant is allowed-in-part.

ii) The judgment and award dated 25.09.2018 passed by the Tribunal viz., MACT,
The Court of Small Causes at Bengaluru in MVC No.4580/2017, is modified.

iii) The claimants are entitled for total revised compensation of Rs. 4,36,196-00 as against Rs.
2,99,196-00 awarded by the Tribunal.

The claimants are entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs. 1,37,720-00 [Rs. 4,36,196 Smt. Saraswathi @ K. Saraswathi vs The National Insurance Company Ltd on 19 April, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/98931947/
6 - Rs.2,99,196] with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

17. Towards 'Medical Expenses' the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,28,716/-, which is on the basis of the actual bills produced by the claimant at Ex.P7 and the same does not call for interference by this Court.

In view of this Court having enhanced the monthly income of the claimant from Rs.8,000/- to Rs.11,000/-
and three months time would be required for the claimant to recuperate and get back to her normal day-to-day activities, Rs.33,000/- is awarded under this head, as against Rs.16,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, I deem it proper to enhance the compensation under this head by another sum of Rs.20,000/-, by making it Rs.40,000/-
Towards 'Attendant Charges, Conveyance, Food and Nourishment charges, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.

the same is retained and not interfered with.
21. Towards 'Future Medical Expenses' the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-.
Hence, I do not find any reason to interfere with the same.
Hence, the compensation amount awarded under this head is not disturbed.
